gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 11?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 11 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Latest ensemble forecasts from the German Weather Service (DWD) and ECMWF place Munich’s August 11 maximum near 29–30 °C.** Afternoon peaks are modulated by variable high-cloud cover and light south-westerly flow that limits full solar heating, keeping surface temperatures from climbing higher. 

Model spreads of 1–2 °C around this central tendency create genuine uncertainty between a 30 °C and 31 °C peak, which is why those two outcomes dominate trader consensus at roughly equal implied probabilities. Recent model runs have shown only minor shifts, with no strong signal for either a clearer sky or increased moisture that would push the maximum notably higher or lower. Official station data will resolve the market based on the single highest reading, making small differences in afternoon boundary-layer mixing and cloud timing the key variables still in play.

eventMetadata.context_description: National Weather Service forecasts and model consensus currently point to a Central Park high of 90–91°F on August 10, driven by southerly flow, moderate humidity, and ample solar heating under limited cloud cover. This places the expected peak several degrees above the long-term August average of 83°F while remaining well within typical mid-summer variability. Trader consensus at near-100% implied probability for the 90–91°F bin reflects tight agreement across recent model runs and morning observations. Afternoon sea-breeze timing or scattered convection could still trim the peak by a degree or two, and any late revisions in official guidance would be the primary factors that could shift the outcome.

Official agencies emphasize that short-range forecasts become highly reliable within 24–48 hours, with resolution based on verified station maxima from the Deutscher Wetterdienst network. Updated model runs and official briefings over the next 48 hours will refine these distinctions ahead of resolution.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 11 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/jp/tokyo/RJTT.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 13 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/jp/tokyo/RJTT.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models from the Japan Meteorological Agency and international sources indicate a maximum temperature in Tokyo on August 13, 2026, most likely between 27–29 °C, reflecting typical mid-August summer conditions moderated by cloud cover and possible showers.** 

High pressure with humid maritime air from the Pacific, combined with Tokyo’s urban heat island effect and limited sea breezes, supports afternoon peaks near 28–29 °C. Minor differences among leading outcomes hinge on the timing and extent of afternoon convection or increased cloudiness, which can suppress daytime maxima by 1–2 °C. Recent JMA guidance and extended forecasts (e.g., timeanddate.com) align closely with this narrow range, producing tight market-implied probabilities as traders weigh the latest model consensus against climatological August averages of 30–33 °C. Updated model runs and official briefings over the next 48 hours will refine these distinctions ahead of resolution.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 12 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: National Weather Service and NOAA model consensus for August 11 positions the daily high near or slightly above the upper 80s at Central Park and LaGuardia, reflecting a warmer-than-average mid-August pattern driven by persistent high pressure, southerly flow, and strong solar insolation under partly sunny skies. With the climatological normal high at 83°F, current guidance incorporates urban heat island effects and elevated humidity that enhance daytime warming while scattered afternoon convection or sea-breeze timing introduces modest uncertainty that could trim the peak by 1–2°F. Recent observations and model runs have kept probabilities concentrated on the 88–91°F range, consistent with the market’s 80% combined implied probability for those bins and limited weighting on extremes. Updated NWS briefings and real-time station data remain the primary near-term variables that could refine the distribution before the official maximum is recorded.

These conditions align with the market's concentration of implied probability on 86-89°F outcomes, which exceed the long-term August normal of 83°F but remain below heat advisory thresholds. Updated short-range model runs tomorrow morning will provide the last key inputs before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment clusters around 28–29°C for Tokyo’s August 13 maximum because short-range models show persistent cloud cover and scattered showers from an approaching typhoon system that is expected to limit daytime heating.** 

Official guidance from the Japan Meteorological Agency and ensemble runs indicate a daily high near 28–30 °C (roughly 82–86 °F) under overcast skies and frequent showers, with 70 % precipitation probability. This pattern contrasts with Tokyo’s August climatology of 30–32 °C under clearer conditions. The typhoon’s outer bands increase low-level moisture and reduce solar insolation, capping the maximum and shifting probability mass toward the lower end of the historical range. 

Ensemble spread remains modest, but any westward shift or weakening of the system could allow brief clearing and push readings toward 31 °C; conversely, heavier or earlier rainfall would favor 27 °C or below. New JMA and global model updates over the next 24–48 hours will refine cloud timing and directly influence the final distribution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent short-range forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and other models indicate mostly cloudy conditions with scattered showers or thunderstorms possible over Tokyo on August 13, 2026, which would limit peak solar heating and keep the daily maximum near 28–30°C.** 

This aligns with the tightly clustered market-implied probabilities centered on 28–29°C (combined ~53%). Typical mid-August climatology features highs of 31–33°C under the influence of the subtropical Pacific high, but current model consensus points to a transient moisture surge or weakened high-pressure ridge that increases cloud cover and precipitation chances, suppressing afternoon temperatures by 2–4°C relative to clear-sky expectations. 

Key differentiating variables include the exact timing and coverage of any showers (earlier or more widespread rain favors the lower end near 28°C; delayed or lighter activity allows a brief push toward 30°C) and boundary-layer moisture levels, which affect both the heat index and the potential for convective cooling. With resolution imminent, traders are weighting the latest JMA updates and ensemble guidance showing modest uncertainty around these thresholds rather than the broader seasonal above-normal signal.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Clear skies and strong solar heating under high-pressure conditions are positioning 30–31°C as the leading outcomes for Munich’s daily maximum on August 11.** Official forecasts from AccuWeather and timeanddate both indicate a high near 30°C (86°F) with mostly sunny conditions, while other models cluster between 28–31°C. These values sit close to or slightly above the long-term August average for the region, reflecting typical late-summer radiative warming without significant cloud cover or advection of cooler air. Traders have concentrated probability on 30°C (55%) and 31°C (42%) because ensemble guidance shows limited spread around this narrow band, with only modest upside risk from delayed cooling or localized urban heat effects. Updated model runs later today will confirm whether the peak reaches the upper end of that range before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Japan Meteorological Agency forecasts indicate Tokyo will see mostly cloudy conditions with scattered showers on August 13, limiting daytime solar heating and supporting maximum temperatures near 28–29 °C. Persistent high humidity from the strengthened Pacific High, combined with urban heat-island effects and modest southerly flow, keeps readings close to seasonal normals of 31.6 °C while cloud cover and precipitation probabilities of 50–70 % suppress further warming. Ensemble model runs show only minor spread in timing of showers, explaining the tight market clustering around 28–29 °C rather than higher outcomes. Updated guidance expected within 24 hours could refine these thresholds ahead of resolution.

Updated observations and final model consensus before evening will determine whether the high settles in the leading bin or edges higher.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Current forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) and other models point to a highest temperature in Tokyo on August 12 of 26–28°C amid widespread showers and cloud cover, which aligns with the market's leading implied probabilities clustered around those values.** 

Persistent moisture from an active weather pattern, including a frontal system or remnant influence, is expected to limit solar heating and keep daytime maxima below the typical late-summer average of 30–32°C. High humidity will still make conditions feel muggy, but the rain and overcast skies reduce the chance of stronger heating that could push readings to 29°C or higher. 

This setup explains the sharp drop in probabilities above 28°C, as ensemble guidance shows limited variability once precipitation begins. Traders are weighting the official JMA outlook and short-range model consensus heavily, with only modest upside risk if clearing occurs earlier than expected. The next model runs and JMA updates through the evening of August 11 will be the key near-term catalysts for any probability shifts.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from the National Weather Service and private sources indicate a daytime high near 88°F in Central Park under partly cloudy skies with a late-afternoon thunderstorm possible, limiting further warming. This aligns with trader consensus favoring the 88-89°F bin at 61% implied probability, ahead of 90-91°F at 20% and 86-87°F at 19.5%. Above-average August conditions, driven by a warmer-than-normal monthly outlook from the Climate Prediction Center, support readings several degrees above the 83°F climatological average, though moderating Atlantic moisture and variable winds introduce uncertainty in peak intensity. Official resolution relies on the NWS daily climatological report, with any model shifts in afternoon heating or convective timing likely to influence final positioning.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models from sources like the UK Met Office currently indicate a daytime maximum near 29°C for Munich on August 12, 2026, aligning closely with the market’s top outcomes clustered at 29–31°C (combined ~93% implied probability).**

This positioning reflects consensus among European and global numerical weather prediction systems, which show stable high-pressure conditions supporting mostly sunny skies and light winds that allow efficient daytime heating without excessive advection of warmer air. Typical August climatology for Munich places average highs near 23–25°C, but the current setup exceeds this baseline modestly due to clear conditions and seasonal insolation.

Short-term model runs exhibit limited spread on peak values, with resolution expected from official DWD station observations that define the exact maximum. Minor uncertainties in afternoon cloud cover or boundary-layer mixing could shift the outcome within the narrow 29–31°C range favored by traders, consistent with the tight probability distribution.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 11 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the London City Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/gb/london/EGLC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office and BBC forecasts indicate London will reach a daily maximum of 25–26°C on August 11 under sunny conditions with light easterly winds and minimal cloud cover, supporting the market’s strong 87.5% implied probability for a 24°C high. Afternoon observations near 22°C at mid-morning align with model consensus that peak temperatures will stay below late-summer averages for the region, while stable high-pressure patterns limit the potential for stronger warming. These conditions explain why probabilities for 26°C and above remain below 1%, as any upward revision would require unexpected shifts in steering flow or insolation not currently indicated by official guidance.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Cloud cover and widespread showers expected across the Kanto region on August 12 are the dominant near-term factors capping Tokyo’s daily maximum temperature.** Official guidance from the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) and ensemble forecasts highlight persistent overcast skies with frequent scattered showers throughout the day, limiting solar heating and keeping the highest reading most likely in the 26–28 °C range. These conditions align with the current market-implied odds, where 27 °C leads at 36.5 % followed by 26 °C at 24.5 % and 28 °C at 19.0 %.

Longer-range seasonal outlooks from JMA continue to indicate above-normal summer temperatures driven by a strong Pacific high, yet the specific synoptic setup for August 12 features sufficient moisture and cloudiness to suppress the peak by several degrees relative to clear-sky climatology. Model spreads remain modest, with most guidance clustering between 26 °C and 28 °C; any break in the rain or earlier clearing could push the high toward 28–29 °C, while heavier or more prolonged precipitation would favor the lower end of the distribution. Traders are therefore pricing modest forecast uncertainty ahead of the next JMA update and observational data on the 12th itself.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Cloud cover and widespread showers expected across the Kanto region on August 12 are the dominant near-term factors capping Tokyo’s daily maximum temperature.** Official guidance from the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) and ensemble forecasts highlight persistent overcast skies with frequent scattered showers throughout the day, limiting solar heating and keeping the highest reading most likely in the 26–28 °C range. These conditions align with the current market-implied odds, where 27 °C leads at 36.5 % followed by 26 °C at 24.5 % and 28 °C at 19.0 %.

Longer-range seasonal outlooks from JMA continue to indicate above-normal summer temperatures driven by a strong Pacific high, yet the specific synoptic setup for August 12 features sufficient moisture and cloudiness to suppress the peak by several degrees relative to clear-sky climatology. Model spreads remain modest, with most guidance clustering between 26 °C and 28 °C; any break in the rain or earlier clearing could push the high toward 28–29 °C, while heavier or more prolonged precipitation would favor the lower end of the distribution. Traders are therefore pricing modest forecast uncertainty ahead of the next JMA update and observational data on the 12th itself.

Updated JMA and ensemble guidance ahead of the date will likely drive further shifts.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Japan Meteorological Agency and global model guidance indicate partly cloudy skies with scattered showers and a strengthening sea breeze for Tokyo on August 13, moderating the daily maximum near the climatological mid-August baseline of 30–32 °C. These conditions, combined with typical 70–80 % humidity and urban heat-island effects, have concentrated trader probabilities on 28 °C (35.5 %) and 29 °C (23.5 %), as afternoon cloud cover and boundary-layer mixing can readily trim or add 1–2 °C. Historical analogs show similar setups frequently produce highs in the upper 20s Celsius when convection develops, while any delay in shower onset would favor the low-30s tail. Updated model runs and JMA briefings through August 12 will remain the key near-term catalysts.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 13 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/jp/tokyo/RJTT.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Japan Meteorological Agency forecasts for Tokyo on August 13 emphasize maximum temperatures near 28°C amid variable cloud cover and scattered showers, driving the 33.5% market-implied odds for that outcome. Seasonal outlooks indicate above-normal warmth from an enhanced Pacific High, yet short-term model runs diverge on precipitation timing and intensity, which can suppress afternoon peaks by several degrees. Historical August baselines average 31–32°C, but current patterns favor moderation around the 27–29°C range reflected in the spread of probabilities. Traders are monitoring the next JMA update and refined ensemble guidance for shifts in land-sea breeze or frontal activity that could tip the daily high.
